column1: # Machine-readable registry of the couplings in COUPLING_AND_INTERFERENCE.md.
# scripts/dccc.sh resolves each symbol at run time and measures statement
# coverage restricted to it. That is the mechanically useful part of DO-178C's
# data- and control-coupling objective: define the interfaces well enough to
# write test cases against them, then measure coverage of the statements that
# cross a component boundary.
# A symbol that cannot be resolved is a refusal, not a skip. A registry that
# silently drops a renamed function reports a coverage number for fewer
# couplings than it claims to cover.
# Column 5 is a STATEMENT-COUNT FLOOR, not a coverage floor. A resolvable symbol
# is not the same thing as a symbol that still contains the coupling: stage 4 of
# ADR 0002 extracted openMmapSnapshot's body into openMmapSnapshotWithFS, and
# the measure reported the one remaining line as 1/1 = 100%, up from 26/33.
# dccc.sh refuses when a site holds fewer statements than this floor. Re-record
# it with 'make dccc-update' when a coupling legitimately changes size. A
# statement count is a property of the code and not of the machine, which is why
# this floor may be taken locally and the coverage floor may not.
# Columns: id
# Column 4 may be qualified as Receiver.Method (e.g. GraphStorage.Foo) when a
# package declares more than one same-named method on different receivers.
# dccc.sh refuses a bare symbol that resolves to more than one file rather
# than silently measuring whichever file its directory glob visits first —
# that silent pick is how C4 measured BTreeGraphStorage.CreateNodeWithTenant
# (no vector code) instead of GraphStorage.CreateNodeWithTenant (the row's own
# note: node creation drives vector index maintenance) until this comment was
# added. Qualify a row the moment a second file declares its symbol; do not
# wait for dccc.sh to catch it.
# NOT YET ENUMERATED: D4, the mmap copy-on-write overlay. A reader materialises
# from the base while a writer promotes into the shard, and no single symbol is
# the boundary. Naming the wrong one would be worse than the gap, so the gap is
# recorded here instead.
